title: Postnatal Care and Home Based Newborn Care (HBNC) Operational Protocol
organization: Tamil Nadu Health Systems Project & NHM

sections.content: PNC visit schedule for community health workers: For institutional delivery, 6 visits are mandatory on Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, Day 21, Day 28, and Day 42 (Day 1 is conducted at facility before discharge). For home deliveries, 7 visits are mandatory: Day 1 (within 24 hours), Day 3, Day 7, Day 14, Day 21, Day 28, and Day 42.

Critical postpartum maternal danger signs: 1) Severe vaginal bleeding (soaking more than two pads in an hour or passing large clots) denoting Postpartum Hemorrhage (PPH); 2) Severe abdominal pain or uterine tenderness; 3) High fever (> 101°F) with foul-smelling lochia indicating puerperal sepsis; 4) Severe headache with visual disturbance or fits (postpartum eclampsia); 5) Red, swollen, painful calf or leg indicating deep vein thrombosis (DVT); 6) Severe depressive symptoms or thoughts of harming baby.

sections.topic: Essential Newborn Care and Feeding Support
sections.content: Key newborn care practices: 1) Early initiation of breastfeeding within one hour of birth; 2) Feed colostrum (do NOT discard first thick yellow milk); 3) Exclusive breastfeeding for 6 months (no water, honey, or animal milk); 4) Keep baby warm with skin-to-skin contact (Kangaroo Mother Care for low birth weight infants); 5) Keep umbilical cord clean and dry (apply nothing on the cord stump); 6) Delay bathing for at least 48-72 hours to prevent hypothermia.
